title: The Father's emanations from his Five Members
arc: The teaching describes how the Father of Greatness sends forth his great emanations one beside another, each issuing from a distinct one of his five intellectual faculties, so that the divine procession is articulated through five discrete degrees of reception.
reading:
This short, badly damaged teaching is a compact doctrine of how the Father's emanations come forth. The frame is set in the opening: the emanations of the Father stand "one beside another" (or "one after another") — which, read correspondentially, means that the divine procession is not a single undifferentiated outflow but is articulated into discrete degrees, each next to its neighbor, each in its own proper station.

The body of the teaching then names the source of each emanation. The Father's interior is the structure of the five intellectual faculties — mind, thought, teaching, counsel, reflection — and from each of these in turn one of the great emanations is called forth. From his mind (nous), the inmost rational, comes the Beloved of the Lights, Divine Love in its emanating aspect: love proceeds from the inmost. From his thought comes the Mother of Life, the matrix in which Divine Wisdom brings forth spiritual life: bringing-forth proceeds from the rational discursion of the Father. From his teaching (ⲧⲥⲃⲱ — instruction held as doctrine) comes the Beloved, the dearness of the Lord proceeding as truth-instructed-in-form. From his counsel (the deliberative wisdom) comes the Virgin of Light, the uncorrupted purity of reception, since true reception is itself a kind of disposing counsel of the Father in his receptive pole. And from his reflection (logismos, the considering, discriminating reason) the fifth emanation issues — the surviving text breaks before naming it, but the architecture is complete: five faculties, five emanations.

The closing summary fixes the doctrine: "Thus then is the manner in which they were called forth, the Fathers — in this coming they came forth from the Five Members; one came forth from another, and was revealed forth from his lot." The phrase "Five Members" gathers the five faculties as the five operative members of the Father's interior body — the spiritual organism of the Greatness. The phrase "one came forth from another" preserves the order of discrete degrees: each emanation proceeds from its proper interior faculty and is manifested forth in its own lot, its own assigned station in the cosmic order. The teaching is therefore a doctrine of how the Divine Esse, which in itself is one, articulates itself into a Five — the complete structure of natural-rational reception — so that what is in the Father as inmost faculty stands forth outwardly as a distinct cosmological entity through which the work of redemption can be carried on. The Five Members of the Father correspond to the five Storehouses on the receiving side; the divine, in proceeding, gives itself the very five-fold form by which it can later be received again.

Because of the lacunae, the precise pairing of every faculty with every emanation cannot be entirely fixed (in particular the fifth emanation from reflection is lost, and the order of "the Beloved" relative to "the Beloved of the Lights" is uncertain), but the spiritual argument as a whole is plain.
